articles.title: Popular “smart drug” Ritalin unexpectedly curbs dishonesty in healthy adults
articles.summary: In a double-blind experiment, healthy adults given the ADHD stimulant methylphenidate cheated far less when nobody was watching, pointing to an unexpected moral side effect of a widely used "smart drug."

articles.title: New psychiatry review finds little consensus on which conditions count as “neurodivergent”
articles.summary: A new JAMA Psychiatry review of 134 studies finds scientists apply "neurodivergent" to 24 distinct diagnoses, from autism and ADHD to anxiety and stroke, raising concerns that broad umbrella labels can mask specific clinical needs.

articles.title: Frequent sleepwalking and sleep terrors at age 4 are linked to more behavioral problems a year later
articles.summary: Sleepwalking and sleep terrors are common in young children and usually harmless. But a Canadian study suggests that when episodes are frequent at age 4, they may go hand in hand with emotional and behavioral difficulties.

articles.title: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental health struggles more strongly than physical or sexual abuse
articles.summary: Childhood emotional abuse leaves no bruises, so it is often dismissed as less harmful than physical or sexual mistreatment. A 104-study analysis in Psychological Bulletin indicates its link to adult mental illness is actually stronger.

articles.title: Machine-learning models can detect elevated psychopathy and sadism from reactions to funny pictures
articles.summary: Your reactions to internet memes and cartoons may carry a hidden personality signal. Researchers trained algorithms on picture ratings and identified elevated psychopathy, sadism, and narcissism, though cold, calculating Machiavellianism left no trace at all.

articles.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. articles.title: Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease
articles.summary: Depression in older adults may be more than a mental health concern. Scientists discovered that accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in people who still had normal memory and thinking abilities. The faster tau built up in the brain, the faster depressive symptoms increased, suggesting that mood changes could emerge before cognitive decline.

articles.title: Study suggests cognitive skills shape how young children learn new words from screen versus paper books
articles.summary: Reading together on paper or an iPad taught preschoolers new words about equally well on average, new research suggests. Yet how well children comprehended words from a screen hinged on their attention, memory, and self-control skills.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between weak bones and faster brain aging
articles.summary: Weakening bones may reveal more about brain health than scientists previously realized, with new research linking lower spinal bone density to faster cognitive decline and accelerated changes in the brain's white matter. The surprising connection suggests that routine medical scans could help uncover hidden warning signs of brain aging and identify people at increased risk of dementia.

Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety a year later, suggesting that consistency could be a key ingredient in protecting mental well-being.

articles.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age
articles.summary: A major analysis of 149 studies found that cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users, with the difference growing to more than six years among adults 30 and older. Researchers warn that cannabis-related psychiatric risks may accumulate over time, challenging the belief that using marijuana after adolescence is relatively safe.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a new genetic eye disease that can silently damage peripheral and night vision while leaving central sight largely unaffected for years. The condition may be detectable through an unusual difficulty adjusting to darkness, offering a potential early warning sign before irreversible retinal damage occurs.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s breakthrough exposes a hidden flaw in the brain’s cleanup system
articles.summary: Scientists have identified a gene that helps the brain’s immune cells contain harmful plaques linked to Alzheimer’s, potentially revealing a new way to fight the disease. When the gene malfunctioned in mice, toxic buildup accelerated and cognitive abilities declined, raising hopes that restoring its function could help protect the brain.

articles.title: A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that a common blood pressure drug can activate calorie-burning brown fat in mice, potentially opening a new path toward improving metabolic health. An analysis of more than 100,000 patients also revealed surprising links between brown fat and lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, anxiety, and depression.

articles.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
articles.summary: A new clinical trial found that the ketogenic diet dramatically outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat diets in reducing liver fat and improving metabolic health, even when participants lost similar amounts of weight. After just four to five months, about half of those following keto no longer met the criteria for prediabetes, while their liver fat dropped by an average of 67%.
